question: Which rule is used to determine the direction of mechanical force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
options: Right-Hand Thumb Rule
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
Fleming's Right-Hand Rule
Ohm's Law
explanation: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule aligns Thumb (Force), Forefinger (Magnetic Field), and Middle finger (Current) perpendicularly.

question: True or False: Two magnetic field lines can intersect each other near magnet poles.

question: Explain the role of Earth wire and Safety Fuse in domestic electric circuits.
options: Earth wire grounds metallic appliance bodies to prevent electric shocks. Fuse wire melts when current exceeds safe limits, breaking the circuit to prevent fires.
By multiplying the given values by the scale factor
By calculating the perimeter using standard formulas
By finding the prime factorization of the given numbers
correct_answer: Earth wire grounds metallic appliance bodies to prevent electric shocks. Fuse wire melts when current exceeds safe limits, breaking the circuit to prevent fires.
explanation: Earth wire provides a zero-resistance safety path to ground; Fuse uses Joule's heating to prevent overcurrent damage.

question: Describe the construction and working principle of an Electric Motor.
options: Principle: Current-carrying armature coil in a magnetic field experiences a rotational force (Fleming's Left-Hand Rule). Commutator split-rings reverse current direction every half rotation to sustain continuous uni-directional torque.
By multiplying the given values by the scale factor
By calculating the perimeter using standard formulas
By finding the prime factorization of the given numbers
correct_answer: Principle: Current-carrying armature coil in a magnetic field experiences a rotational force (Fleming's Left-Hand Rule). Commutator split-rings reverse current direction every half rotation to sustain continuous uni-directional torque.
explanation: Commutator segments P-Q flip current polarity in armature sides AB and CD twice per full cycle.

question: A 5.5 kW commercial air conditioner operating on 220 V AC is connected to a circuit protected by a 15 A fuse. Analyze what will happen when the AC is switched on.
options: Current drawn I = P / V = 5500 W / 220 V = 25 Amperes. Since 25 A exceeds the 15 A fuse rating, the fuse wire will instantly melt and break the circuit.
By multiplying the given values by the scale factor
By calculating the perimeter using standard formulas
By finding the prime factorization of the given numbers
correct_answer: Current drawn I = P / V = 5500 W / 220 V = 25 Amperes. Since 25 A exceeds the 15 A fuse rating, the fuse wire will instantly melt and break the circuit.
explanation: Excess current (25 A vs 15 A limit) triggers excessive Joule heating (I^2Rt) in fuse element, melting it to prevent domestic wiring overload.
